blueprints.correctNucleus: πέπαυται has secure perfect-middle parsing; that parsing alone does not prove sinless perfection.
distractorFamilies: perfect tense automatically means permanent sinlessness
the verb can only mean physical death
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Every option must distinguish a real grammatical or exegetical inference; no caricature of holiness theology.

blueprints.correctNucleus: Atkinson treats ἐν ᾧ in 4:4 causally; the construction does not have one mechanical function everywhere in 1 Peter.
distractorFamilies: one fixed English gloss in every occurrence
causal force derived from morphology alone
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Attribute Atkinson specifically; do not present abstract-level analysis as consensus.

blueprints.correctNucleus: νεκροῖς and εὐηγγελίσθη do not by morphology settle when or where the gospel was preached; serious interpretations remain.
distractorFamilies: aorist passive proves preaching while alive
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Challenge may ask what the grammar does NOT prove, but must not ask which disputed interpretation is certainly correct.

blueprints.correctNucleus: ἤγγικεν is secure perfect morphology; the verse's explicit response is sober prayer, not a complete eschatological timetable.
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Project eschatology may be discussed only as project-level synthesis, never as the lexical answer.

blueprints.correctNucleus: 1 Pet 4:8 strongly reuses a proverbial/scriptural maxim but visibly differs from LXX Prov 10:12 and should not be called mechanical verbatim quotation.
distractorFamilies: direct MT translation proven by wording alone
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Wrong options should differ in reuse classification, not in unrelated verse references.

blueprints.correctNucleus: Speaking and serving organize the exhortation around stewardship and God's glory; the passage does not state that exactly two gifts exist.
distractorFamilies: divine strength removes human responsibility to serve
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Do not force cessationism/continuationism into a direct-text card.

blueprints.correctNucleus: Stable base-text content and morphology can be taught while the expanded Spirit/glory textual unit remains apparatus HOLD.
distractorFamilies: variant expansion is part of checked base text
one disputed phrase makes whole verse unusable
blueprints.fairnessGuard: The correct answer must never require uninspected witness distribution.

blueprints.correctNucleus: Χριστιανός is real social-historical evidence but does not by itself choose Nero/Domitian/Trajan or one official empire-wide persecution regime.
distractorFamilies: term has no historical value at all
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Do not turn Byrley's preferred persecution model into consensus.

blueprints.correctNucleus: 4:18 is a very close LXX reproduction and is materially stronger as quotation-level reuse than 4:8.
distractorFamilies: close wording proves salvation by works
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Separate the textual relationship from theological interpretation of μόλις.

blueprints.correctNucleus: The shepherding command and anti-domination ethics are stable; advanced claims built on ἐπισκοποῦντες or κατὰ θεόν remain apparatus-sensitive.
distractorFamilies: ποιμάνατε alone proves complete denominational polity
blueprints.fairnessGuard: No witness list may appear unless exact ECM/critical apparatus was inspected.

blueprints.correctNucleus: The reuse is very close but changes the subject from κύριος in LXX to ὁ θεός in 1 Peter; the motive for that adaptation is not established by the wording alone.
distractorFamilies: subject change proves a known authorial motive
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Test visible wording, not speculative motive.

blueprints.correctNucleus: Casting anxiety is tied to humility and God's care; the text does not say a faithful believer never feels anxiety or must refuse human help.
distractorFamilies: seeking help contradicts casting care on God
participle parsing alone proves every syntactic nuance
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Avoid mental-health shaming disguised as a Bible question.

blueprints.correctNucleus: The adversary/devil and roaring-lion metaphor are explicit; one exclusive Jewish, Greco-Roman, arena, or OT background is not textually mandatory.
distractorFamilies: one OT lion passage is grammatically required
ad bestias is established as the single source
because devil is named the lion image has no background significance
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Hallstrom remains abstract/opening-bounded; Byrley is one full evangelical study, not consensus.

blueprints.correctNucleus: διὰ Σιλουανοῦ does not by itself prove that Silvanus composed the Greek as Peter's secretary; carrier and amanuensis models require historical argument.
distractorFamilies: polished Greek proves Silvanus composed the letter
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Richards/NET preferences must be attributed, not converted into neutral fact.

blueprints.correctNucleus: Βαβυλών is the written place-name and συνεκλεκτή is feminine singular; Rome identification and church/woman referent are historical-exegetical questions, not morphology.
distractorFamilies: three historical location theories imply equal probability
blueprints.fairnessGuard: Do not make a disputed historical identification a faithfulness test.

blueprints.correctNucleus: A responsible advanced learner should know that the now-dead-after-lifetime-evangelization reading has substantial support, while Horrell 2003 defends a serious postmortem-proclamation alternative; course closure remains HOLD.
distractorFamilies: all serious scholarship agrees on now-dead reading
all serious scholarship agrees on postmortem preaching
one recent CC article settles the issue
blueprints.fairnessGuard: This may become a dispute-awareness card, never a competitive 'which interpretation is true?' card while the project position is HOLD.
